My expectation is that this will be redundant with VPN controls on the extension, but they make sense, and it's OK to have them.

The other thing related to this UI that is worth exploring are different shield states. Right now, when the extension excludes a website, we show an icon in the right of the URL bar: https://www.figma.com/design/s13B7zs27cadZXUyvxobgW/Mozilla-VPN-Extension?node-id=3846-99240&t=TFpe2g4dRkUwN4F6-4. Likewise, when a location is set, we show a flag. But in both situations, we are doing this because as an extension we can't touch the shield icon, which I think would be a better place.

So how can we convey, through the shield icon if a website is ETP enabled, ETP disabled, VPN protected, VPN unprotected or with a VPN geo-override?

@Jamie Sigadel @Sally Richardson @Jennifer Palais

Love this concept. "Felt privacy" was all the rage a bit ago. But on top of informing users of some stats, this can be a launchpad into our products.

First off: I think we might want to aspire to have a unified dashboard that covers all forms of protection (including ETP, VPN, Relay and Monitor). Some metrics maybe show all the time, and others only show if the user has opted into a given product.

We could think about a bunch of metrics.

Right off the bat, I hypothesize that a metric that says "% of web traffic encrypted" could be compelling because (a) without doing anything the user will already be at 90% or so simply because most websites are https - this is actually good because it's proven that being close (but not there) to completion is what's most likely to lead users to take action (b) we can have a subtle tooltip that tells them all the ways to improve this, which include not just VPN but also free features like "https only" from Firefox Settings.

For Relay we could have "Emails masks used". If they are on Relay phone, we could say "Phone calls masked", etc. A button to 'manage' could take them to the Relay dashboard.

For Monitor, it could be something positive like "Email addresses" monitored, OR maybe just a checkbox to indicate that their email is protected. Tony will have better ideas.

Jenn - this might be a great cross-product surface for us (a better fit for your product mind than mine).

@Sally Richardson @Jamie Sigadel

In the case of VPN, it would be something along the lines of "You are visiting an insecure website", with a subtext that would explain why, why it matters, and explains how Mozilla VPN can help.

(and again, we should have a way to disable all notifications of this kind... Relay has this on the Relay mask offer, so we probably follow that pattern).

@Jamie Sigadel @Sally Richardson

@Jamie Sigadel @Sally Richardson

(context: These are explorations of VPN entry points on when on an insecure network)

I think these treatments are cool but I do wonder if they are too interruptive. It might be good to have one in our back pockets where the user sees a doorhanger with some messaging, as it was previously mocked for a previous experiment (which didn't launch for content related reasons). Alternatively, one that displays like we do the in-product surveys (a treatment that pops up from the bottom right). OR lastly, maybe a butter bar approach.

In all cases, we do want to make sure that there is an option to dismiss and never see this again.

This UI proposal does create an interesting opportunity, which is that of starting a free trial right there and then with the switch of a button. We could do this, presumably if the user is logged in, and they are eligible for a VPN trial (to avoid gaming).

Freemium is a bigger topic but since this concept is pretty much at the doorstep, it might be to give it some finishing touches to show how it changes the game.
